Buy a Chinese Residence Permit on Telegram

Somebody is selling a Chinese residence permit on Telegram right now and the advert almost certainly quotes a price below 1500–4800 CNY. Whether that price is honest depends on what is in the envelope, not on how confident the seller sounds.

Document type
A residence permit is the card a country issues to a foreign national it has allowed to live there for a fixed term. It sits between a visa and permanent residence.

buy chinese residence permit on telegram – the short version

The band you should expect for a Chinese residence permit is 1500–4800 CNY. Below the bottom you are buying a print and should be told so. Above the top you should be getting a number that was registered rather than invented.

The figure above is a range rather than a quote, and it moves with stock and season. Hold it in your head as a filter, not as a target, and treat every deviation as a claim to be tested.

Buy a Residence Permit via Telegram: how the transaction works

Payment is usually a transfer or a crypto address and neither is reversible. Split it: a deposit for the data page photo, the balance against a tracking number that moves.

A live video call is worth ten photos. Ask the seller to hold the card to a window in daylight and tilt it slowly. The ghost image and the laminate edge are both visible on a call and neither can be staged with a print.

Who actually issues a Residence Permit

the National Immigration Administration is the body to check against. If a seller cannot name the office that issued the document in the photo, the photo is probably borrowed from a stock gallery.

Where no public route exists, the physical checks carry all the weight. That is not ideal, but it is the honest position and any seller who claims otherwise is overselling.

Replica or registered original

A registered original is a document whose number sits in the office records. It may still be a genuine book with your details typed in, but the number resolves, and that is the whole difference in value.

That is why the number should be requested before any payment. If a seller sends the number first and invites you to check it, you are talking to somebody confident about the register.

What a fair price looks like

The bottom of the 1500–4800 CNY band buys a data page print. The middle buys correct stock and the right print method. The top buys a number that resolves at the National Immigration Administration. Ask which one is quoted.

Delivery is part of the price and worth separating. Tracked delivery costs the seller money, and a quote that excludes it is not comparable to one that includes it.

The buying process, step by step

The sequence below is the one that keeps you protected. Run it in order and do not skip ahead to payment.

  1. Ask which office issued it and confirm the answer is the National Immigration Administration.
  2. Request an uncropped photo of the full card on a plain surface with the laminate edge in frame.
  3. Request a UV shot of the data page and a close crop of the number field.
  4. Test the number against the format the National Immigration Administration uses. A number that breaks the format ends the deal.
  5. Agree a price inside the 1500–4800 CNY band and pay in two parts, deposit then balance against tracking.
  6. On arrival check the document against the photos before you accept delivery and photograph the unopened envelope.

Checks that catch bad stock

Run these before money moves. Each one targets a feature that survives handling but not a photocopier.

  • Check the resident identity card for the eighteen digit number and its ISO seven thousand sixty four checksum.
  • Confirm the passport emblem printing and the machine-readable zone.
  • Check the number format against the published rule for the National Immigration Administration. Constructed numbers cannot be invented by hand.
  • Look for the UV print with a 365 nanometre torch. Real ink is sharp and placed deliberately. A print shows a dull bloom or nothing.
  • Loupe the microprint and the ghost image. Both collapse into a dotted line or a grey patch on a photocopy.
  • Compare the data across every field for internal consistency. A postcode that contradicts the state or the office area is a tell.
  • Check the laminate or polycarbonate edge for a fused seal rather than a cut line under a laid sheet.

Red flags that should end the conversation

These end a Chinese residence permit conversation for good.

  • A resident identity card whose eighteen digit number fails the checksum.
  • The seller cannot name the issuing office, only the country.
  • The number breaks the published format, or is round and repeating.

Frequently asked questions

What does a residence permit cost on Telegram?

Between 300 and 1400 US dollars. The permit number and the register entry carry most of the value.

How is it different from a visa?

A visa gets you in. A permit lets you stay. They are issued by different offices and checked differently.

Does it replace a green card?

Outside the United States it is the equivalent tier below permanent residence, not a replacement for it.

Why so expensive?

Because the number has to sit in an immigration register to be worth anything, and that is the hardest part to fake.

What is the common failure?

A permit class that sounds plausible but does not exist in the country scheme. Check the class list first.

Before you pay

Print the checklist, run it in order and pay only at the end. That is the whole method for a Chinese residence permit.
